output.headline: Pete Byrne, Naked Eyes frontman who took British new wave into the US Top 10, dies aged 74
output.standfirst: Singer, whose duo’s cover of Always Something There to Remind Me reached the Top 10 and was followed by Promises, Promises and more US hits, died peacefully in Los Angeles after a brief illness
output.bodyHtml:
Pete Byrne, who as frontman of the British new wave group Naked Eyes carried them to repeated chart successes in the US, has died aged 74.

Byrne died peacefully in Los Angeles on 14 September after a brief illness, the band’s website and social media announced on Wednesday.

Byrne was among the acts of the “second British invasion”, when synthpop and new wave bands from the UK, powered in part by the rise of MTV, swept into the US alongside peers including Duran Duran, A Flock of Seagulls and more.

Naked Eyes was the group he formed in the late 1970s after the failure of his groups Studio and Neon – Neon featuring future Tears for Fears members Curt Smith and Roland Orzabal as well as his future Naked Eyes bandmate Rob Fisher and others. “Rob and I found that running a band was not as interesting as writing and recording,” Byrne said. “We decided to go back to square one.”

As a duo under the new name, they signed to EMI, and their debut single became their biggest hit: a cover of the Burt Bacharach-penned Always Something There to Remind Me, powered by Byrne’s earnest boyish croon, which reached the Top 10 in the US, Canada and Australia.

Naked Eyes went on to three more Top 40 hits in the US – Promises, Promises (which reached No 11 and featured Madonna on unreleased remixes), When the Lights Go Out and (What) In the Name of Love (which was remixed by Arthur Baker) – though they never hit the Top 40 in their native UK.

The duo split after their second album, 1984’s Fuel for the Fire, having been unable to replicate their synth-heavy studio setup on tour. Byrne later put the split down to him and Fisher living in Los Angeles and London respectively, and to EMI losing faith in the project.

Byrne stepped back, writing and producing with other artists – later including a song for Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen – and recorded backing vocals for Stevie Wonder’s 1985 US No 1 Part-Time Lover. He released a solo album, The Real Illusion, in 2001, and began working with Fisher again, rebooting Naked Eyes as a solo project after Fisher’s death in 1999. Under that name Byrne released two further albums and became a familiar face on 80s revue tours, alongside the likes of the Go-Go’s and the Human League.

Music, Byrne said in 2017, has been “the main focus of my life since I was 18. Nothing has changed really. I still get up in the morning, make coffee, fiddle around on the guitar and scribble down some nonsense. And I eventually look back and say: ‘There might be something there.’”

He is survived by three children, Merlin, Dylan and Chloe, from his marriage to ex-wife Elena, and by his siblings Eileen, Sandy, Carol and Steve.
